provenance: 75 instances (24 base scenarios at three feature-noise levels plus three control instances) swept across 19 MLP methods. Executed by 14 parallel single-threaded workers writing one shard per instance; the merged summary was verified to contain all 75 instances, 19 methods and the correct 20 seeds each. Discovery read only the 42 discovery instances; confirmation was executed once.
consequence: Direct progression to Qwen is PROHIBITED; mechanistic investigation resumes on synthetic scenarios

post_hoc_diagnostics.note: POST-HOC. Not pre-registered, changes no verdict, and may not be quoted as a result. Recorded because it localises the failure.

interpretation_limits: NOT CONFIRMED. The pre-registered predictor -- alpha as measured by the frozen Jacobian estimator -- does not predict the frontier advantage under the MLP. Confirmation rho = +0.2089, CI [-0.1705, +0.5329]: wrong sign against the inherited negative expectation, and the interval spans zero.

The frontier advantage itself SURVIVES non-linearity. 40 of 42 discovery instances and 26 of 30 confirmation instances show a positive bias-corrected advantage. What failed is the predictor, not the effect.

Post-hoc, the failure localises to the ESTIMATOR rather than to alpha as a structural quantity: the discrete aliasing index still correlates with the advantage under the MLP (-0.6581 on discovery, -0.3445 on confirmation with CI [-0.6505, +0.0180]), while the Jacobian estimator tracks it only weakly (+0.1724 discovery, +0.5862 confirmation). This is a lead for a successor protocol, NOT a result: it is computed after seeing the outcome, the confirmation-set discrete-alpha interval includes zero, and substituting a different predictor post hoc is exactly what this protocol forbids.

The estimator failure matters more than it looks. On a transformer there is no discrete alpha to fall back on, so a working estimator is mandatory, not optional. Stage B has shown the current one does not work even on an MLP.
The measurement is not degenerate: measured alpha spans 0.31 to 0.81 with a median seed-to-seed SD of 0.030, so the null is not an artefact of a constant or noise-dominated predictor.
The calibration gate passed at 1.11e-16, so the estimator is correct where the discrete answer is defined. Its failure is specific to the non-linear parameterization.
